answer: Each agent must lock a bond in a public vault for 30 days before it can bid for work, and the contract permits only one active identity per bond. Agents can wander between markets, but each additional identity needs fresh collateral. A swarm of 10,000 identities therefore ties up 10,000 bonds, costing the attacker capital and forgone interest. A polished profile may look like a pearl, but it cannot substitute for the deposit.
